fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. God "…through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him." Think about walking past a bakery. You don't need a sign, your nose already knows something good is going on in there. That's the kind of thing Paul is describing, something you can smell from a distance.

Titus it is, friend. Paul says, "I had no peace in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there." A door stood open for the gospel in Troas, and still Paul says he had no peace. I think that tells you how much Titus mattered to him.

Life is the word. Paul says, "To the one we are an odor that brings death, to the other a fragrance that brings life." Same aroma going out, two different results. That's the contrast the whole verse turns on.

I see why Jerusalem came to mind, friend, but Paul doesn't mention it anywhere in this passage. I've picked the wrong ingredient plenty of times in my own bakery, so no worries. He says to the Corinthians, "You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts…" The letter is the people he's writing to.
That's what Paul says. The letter is "…written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God…" No pen and no ink here, friend. The Spirit of the living God is the One who writes it.
Hearts, friend. Paul says the letter is written "…not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts." Stone on one side, human hearts on the other. The letter from Christ is written on people.
That's what Paul says. He writes, "Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God." It's honest. He points the credit straight at God.
